is_anopheles.evidence: The paper focuses on Anopheles gambiae (page 1, Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (kdr-west) and Vgsc L995S (kdr-east) (page 2, Background; Table 1).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 2 provides individual genotype results (SS, RR, RS) for 12 wild-caught specimens.

african_field_population.evidence: Specimens were collected from Asembo, Kenya (field-caught) and Odumasi, Ghana (field-caught) (page 2, Methods; page 4, Table 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study developing and testing a new genotyping method on field and laboratory specimens.

sub_country_location.evidence: The paper specifies Asembo, Kenya and Odumasi, Ghana (page 2, Methods; page 4, Table 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collection dates are specified as May 2004 for Kenya and June 2003 for Ghana (page 2, Methods).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes a new methodology and uses specific samples for validation; there is no indication these samples were previously published as a dataset.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data is contained within the provided PDF.

assessment.summary: This paper presents a new Hot Ligation Oligonucleotide Assay (HOLA) for detecting kdr mutations (L995F and L995S) in Anopheles gambiae. It validates the method using field-collected samples from Kenya and Ghana, comparing results against conventional multiplex PCR.
